Android's clipboard provider is `com.rungic.clipboard.ClipboardDaemon`. Magisk runs it as Shell, UID 2000. The Linux consumer is `shared/platform/clipboard.py` (`rungic-plasma-clipboard`). It synchronizes the clipboard with the Wayland selection through `wl-copy` and `wl-paste`.

The transport uses the abstract Unix socket `com.rungic.clipboard.v1`. Each direction sends one JSON object per line. Each connection carries one request. The consumer checks `SO_PEERCRED` and refuses a server whose UID is not 2000. The daemon answers clients with UID 0, UID 1000, or the app's UID.

The contract permits only plain text. The limits are 65536 characters and 262144 UTF-8 bytes. A `clipboard-get` reply with `available: false` leaves the Linux selection unchanged. Its reason is `locked-or-other-user`, `sensitive`, `non-text` or `too-large`. A null `text` value means Android's clipboard is empty.

The `watch` action waits for a clipboard version change or a daemon restart. A restart changes the epoch. The wait lasts at most `timeout` milliseconds. Errors use {"error": string}.

`tools/tests/test_contract_clipboard.py` checks the real consumer against the substitute in `tools/contracts.py`. The test uses substitutes for `wl-copy` and `wl-paste`. Acceptance scenario `contract.clipboard` checks the daemon on the phone. That check blanks text on the phone and never returns it to the development machine.
